prompt: How does Hono compose middleware? Walk me through what happens between `app.use(...)` calls and a handler being invoked: where the chain is built, where it's dispatched, and the order of execution for `await next()`. Cite file:line.
Where does Hono compile path patterns into matchers? Trace from `router.add(method, path, handler)` to wherever the regex/trie is actually built. Cite file:line for each step.
How does the built-in CORS middleware decide which response headers to set on a preflight (OPTIONS) request vs an actual request? Cite file:line and describe the branching.
Walk me through how the AWS Lambda adapter converts a Lambda event into a Web Request and the Hono Response back into a Lambda result. Cite file:line for both directions.
Hono ships RegExpRouter, TrieRouter, LinearRouter, PatternRouter, and SmartRouter. What are the differences between them and when does each get used? Cite file:line for each implementation.
Where is JWT signing implemented in Hono and which algorithms are supported out of the box? Cite file:line for the algorithm dispatch.
How do `c.json()`, `c.text()`, and `c.html()` differ in the headers they set and where are they each defined? Cite file:line and describe the content-type handling.
How does the context-storage middleware share `Context` across async boundaries? Where is `AsyncLocalStorage` (or its equivalent) set up and accessed? Cite file:line.
When a request comes in, how does Hono decide whether to parse the body as FormData, JSON, or text? Where is that dispatch and what content-types route to which parser? Cite file:line.

If I wanted to add a new built-in middleware so consumers can `import { x } from 'hono/x'`, what's the convention? Where would the source live, where do exports get wired, and what files do I need to touch? Cite file:line for one existing middleware as the example.

Add a new built-in middleware `bodyCap` to `src/middleware/body-cap/index.ts`. Signature: `bodyCap(options: { maxBytes: number }) => MiddlewareHandler`. Reads the request's `Content-Length` header; if present and exceeds `maxBytes`, throw `HTTPException(413, { message: 'Body too large' })` before calling `next()`. Otherwise call `next()`. Follow Hono's middleware factory convention. The project must still typecheck via `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.build.json`.

Add a new built-in middleware `requestTime` to `src/middleware/request-time/index.ts`. Signature: `requestTime() => MiddlewareHandler`. Records `Date.now()` before calling `next()`, and after `next()` resolves, sets the response header `X-Response-Time-Ms` to the elapsed milliseconds (integer). Use the `MiddlewareHandler` type from `src/types.ts`. The project must typecheck via `tsconfig.build.json`.

Add a new built-in middleware `languageTag` to `src/middleware/language-tag/index.ts`. Signature: `languageTag(options: { allowed: string[]; default: string }) => MiddlewareHandler`. Parses `c.req.header('Accept-Language')`, picks the highest-q language tag from `options.allowed`, falls back to `options.default`, and sets it on the request via `c.set('language', tag)`. Then `await next()`. Use `MiddlewareHandler`. Project must typecheck.

Add a new built-in middleware `ifNoneMatch` to `src/middleware/if-none-match/index.ts`. Signature: `ifNoneMatch() => MiddlewareHandler`. After `await next()`, if the response has an `ETag` header AND the request's `If-None-Match` header matches it (exact string match), replace the response with a 304 Not Modified and an empty body, preserving the `ETag` header. Use the `MiddlewareHandler` type. Project must typecheck.

Add a new built-in middleware `health` to `src/middleware/health/index.ts`. Signature: `health(options?: { path?: string; status?: 'ok' | 'degraded' }) => MiddlewareHandler`. If `c.req.path === (options?.path ?? '/healthz')`, short-circuit by returning `c.json({ status: options?.status ?? 'ok' }, 200)` immediately (do not call `next()`). Otherwise call `next()`. Use `MiddlewareHandler`. Project must typecheck.

Add a new helper module `request-info` at `src/helper/request-info/index.ts`. Export a single function `getRequestInfo(c: Context) => { method: string; path: string; query: Record<string, string>; headers: Record<string, string> }`. `query` should be the parsed query string as flat key/value, `headers` should be all request headers lower-cased. Import `Context` from `../../context`. The project must typecheck via `tsconfig.build.json`.

Add a new helper module `bearer` at `src/helper/bearer/index.ts`. Export `getBearerToken(c: Context) => string | null`. Reads the `Authorization` header from `c.req` and returns the token portion if it starts with `Bearer ` (case-insensitive scheme), otherwise `null`. Import `Context` from `../../context`. Project must typecheck.

Add a new helper module `clear-cookies` at `src/helper/clear-cookies/index.ts`. Export `clearAllCookies(c: Context) => void`. Reads every cookie from the request via `c.req.header('Cookie')`, parses cookie names, and for each one calls `setCookie(c, name, '', { maxAge: 0 })` using the existing `setCookie` from `src/helper/cookie`. Import `Context` from `../../context` and `setCookie` from `../cookie`. Project must typecheck.

Add a new method `notModified()` on the `Context` class in `src/context.ts`. Signature: `notModified(): Response`. Returns a `Response` with status 304 and an empty body, going through the existing `this.newResponse(...)` / `this.body(...)` path so headers merge correctly. Place it next to the existing `redirect` / `json` / `text` methods. Project must typecheck via `tsconfig.build.json`.

Add a new method `problem(detail: { type?: string; title: string; status: number; detail?: string })` on the `Context` class in `src/context.ts`. Signature: `problem(detail: { type?: string; title: string; status: number; detail?: string }): Response`. Returns an RFC 7807 Problem Details response: body is JSON of `detail`, content-type is `application/problem+json`, status is `detail.status`. Route through the existing `this.newResponse(...)` / `this.body(...)` infrastructure to preserve header merging. Place it near the existing `json` method. Project must typecheck.
